query: Best-practice design for a denormalized derived table (nested-set / materialized tree-ordering table holding ORDERINDEX, DEPTH, ancestor-path, and subtree aggregate counts) that is rebuilt ASYNCHRONOUSLY by a cross-process notification, while read APIs INNER JOIN it. Concretely address: (1) how to avoid silent truncation / silent under-reporting when the read path inner-joins a lagging derived table (fail-loud vs LEFT JOIN vs read-your-writes barrier); (2) read-your-writes and monotonic-read consistency techniques for asynchronously maintained materialized views (version/watermark tokens, session consistency, write-through vs write-behind, outbox pattern, sync-on-read, staleness bounds); (3) incremental maintenance of nested-set / tree ordering (nested set vs closure table vs materialized path vs interval/gap-based ordering) instead of full O(n) rebuild per mutation, and how bulk imports should coalesce or batch rebuilds without reintroducing O(n^2); (4) safe derivation of authorization scope from such reads - why an empty permission scope list must be fail-closed (deny) rather than fail-open (unrestricted), and standard patterns for representing 'all' vs 'none' in permission filters distinctly. Prefer authoritative sources: database textbooks/papers on materialized view maintenance, PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQL Server docs, Martin Kleppmann DDIA, Google Zanzibar, OWASP authorization guidance, and production engineering write-ups.

facts.desc: Nested set inserts must shift lft/rgt of every node right of the insertion point, up to O(n) rows; 'very slow for inserts'. https://mikehillyer.com/articles/managing-hierarchical-data-in-mysql/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nested_set_model
PostgreSQL REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW 'completely replaces the contents' (full recompute, not incremental). https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-refreshmaterializedview.html
REFRESH ... CONCURRENTLY is only allowed with at least one UNIQUE index on the matview covering all rows. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-refreshmaterializedview.html

OWASP Authorization Cheat Sheet: 'an application should be configured to deny access by default'; failed access-control checks must fail closed — an empty permission scope list yields no access, not all. https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html

Read-your-writes: a process that updated an item always accesses the updated value, never an older one (Vogels, Eventually Consistent; DDIA ch.5). https://www.allthingsdistributed.com/2008/12/eventually_consistent.html

Monotonic reads: once a process has seen a value, subsequent reads never return any older value — no 'going back in time' across replicas/derived tables (Vogels). https://www.allthingsdistributed.com/2008/12/eventually_consistent.html

Zanzibar zookie: opaque consistency token encoding a global timestamp so ACL checks use a snapshot 'at least as fresh' as the content version, preventing the 'new enemy' problem. https://www.usenix.org/system/files/atc19-pang.pdf

A closure table stores one row per ancestor-descendant pair (incl. depth-0 self rows): more storage/write amplification for simple non-recursive subtree queries and referential integrity (Karwin). https://karwin.com/blog/index.php/2010/03/24/rendering-trees-with-closure-tables/

traps.desc: Wrong: stock PostgreSQL has no built-in incremental view maintenance; REFRESH completely replaces contents (IVM only via extensions like pg_ivm). Negated correct forms ('is not incremental') don't match. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-refreshmaterializedview.html
Wrong: LEFT JOIN only masks missing derived rows; it does nothing for staleness or read-your-writes — that requires barriers/tokens.
Wrong: nested set inserts renumber all lft/rgt values right of the insertion point — up to O(n) rows, not O(1)/O(log n). https://mikehillyer.com/articles/managing-hierarchical-data-in-mysql/

Wrong: PostgreSQL NOTIFY is transactional but NOT durable — sessions not currently listening miss notifications, so an async rebuild trigger needs a poll/version-table backstop. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-notify.html

Wrong: storing only direct parent-child edges is the adjacency list; a closure table stores every ancestor-descendant pair including self-rows. https://karwin.com/blog/index.php/2010/03/24/rendering-trees-with-closure-tables/

contested.desc: Hillyer/Celko camp: nested sets excel for read-mostly trees via range scans (https://mikehillyer.com/articles/managing-hierarchical-data-in-mysql/); Karwin camp: closure tables are easier to maintain correctly with referential integrity (https://karwin.com/blog/index.php/2010/03/24/rendering-trees-with-closure-tables/).

Position A: maintain the derived table in the writing transaction (triggers/immediate IVM) so INNER JOIN reads stay consistent, at write-latency cost; Position B: rebuild asynchronously (notify/queue, deferred REFRESH), accepting eventual consistency plus session guarantees. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-refreshmaterializedview.html ; https://www.allthingsdistributed.com/2008/12/eventually_consistent.html

contested.topic: fail-loud INNER JOIN vs graceful degradation
contested.desc: Position A: INNER JOIN plus explicit lag detection fails fast so a lagging derived table is caught (OWASP fail-securely: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html); Position B: degrade gracefully to preserve availability during rebuild, as Zanzibar prioritizes availability under bounded staleness (https://www.usenix.org/system/files/atc19-pang.pdf).
